title: Progressive collapse and interaction resilience for Cost breakdowns & Rollout modals
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create and validate a set of responsive layout rules and interaction polish for the Cost Breakdown pages and Rollout modal flows. Focus areas: progressive column collapse for tabular cost views, lightweight card reflow for summary dashboards, resilient chart canvas fallbacks for WebKit/Firefox, and modal stacking/keyboard focus behavior for rollout actions. Goal is consistent layout and interaction across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge at 320px–2560px widths and on touch devices.
acceptance_criteria: Cost table applies progressive column priority rules at <640px, 640–1024px, >1024px and never requires horizontal scrolling for the primary billing row
Dashboard cost cards reflow to 1/2/3-column grids per breakpoint and preserve CTA visibility (Deploy / Cancel / View details)
Charts degrade to SVG sparkline fallback if canvas measurements differ on Safari retina devices; no layout shift observed on initial paint
Rollout modal remains centered, respects safe-area insets, supports keyboard trap + ESC to close, and stacks correctly when multiple modals are opened (z-index and inertness behavior validated)
All implemented changes pass cross-browser regression checklist and have automated Percy snapshots for 12 breakpoints
Design review sign-off from PM, Eng, and Accessibility (a11y) with follow-up tickets created for any compromises
notes: Trade-off: hiding low-priority columns on narrow widths may reduce visibility for advanced billing use-cases; created a 'dense view' toggle for power users as a follow-up
Prefer CSS grid with named areas for card reflow to keep animations GPU-friendly and avoid JS-driven layout shifts
Avoid aggressive token-level truncation; use secondary meta rows inside cards to keep primary numbers visible
decisions: Adopt progressive column priority system (primary, secondary, tertiary). Primary columns never collapse; secondary collapse to stacked rows; tertiary hidden behind 'More' pill
Chart fallback: keep canvas for Chrome/Firefox; render a precomputed SVG sparkline for Safari retina and for snapshot tests to improve visual stability
Modal stacking: adopt 'inert' attribute polyfill for browsers without native support and enforce a max stack depth of 2 active modals

cross_browser_issues: Safari (macOS/iOS): canvas.getBoundingClientRect rounding on retina causes 1px hairline shifts — mitigated by using integer snap and SVG fallback
Firefox: subpixel antialiasing difference on small sparkline strokes; normalize by exporting 1px stroke as 2px scaled SVG in snapshot builds
Edge: scroll chaining inside nested modals on touch requires overscroll-behavior: contain
rollout_impact: Low to medium. UI-only change behind feature flag. Coordinate with rollout service to avoid showing in-app rollout actions during initial canary if any server-side UX hooks change.
qa_checks: Run Percy visual snapshots against feature flag enabled/disabled states
Keyboard-only nav for modals and tables validated with VoiceOver and NVDA
Mobile touch target sizes >= 44px for primary CTAs
accessibility_considerations: Ensure collapsed columns have accessible 'More' button with aria-expanded and aria-controls
Modal open: focus moved to first interactive element and previous focus restored on close
Color contrast for cost deltas meets 4.5:1 for normal text; use icons + text rather than color alone
